title: Index bits leave the width state unchanged
statement: For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, every counter value $c\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, and every Boolean flag $g$, folding the width-pass transition over a string of $n$ consecutive $1$ bits, starting in state $2$ with counter $c$ and flag $g$, returns the same state, counter, and flag.
replaced:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every counter value $c$, and every flag $g$, folding
the width-pass transition over the unary run $1^n$ from the index position with
counter $c$ and flag $g$ returns exactly the same state: index bits change neither
the position, nor the counter, nor the flag.
